pair_dispositions.reason: 6 owns strongest win conversion; 4 has best independent second path from stable consistency and prior placings.
7 has strong 1200 Funabashi line and can fill second if 1200 race shape dominates over 4's solidity.
1 brings stronger outside-company form and may hold for second if course transfer works immediately.
If 6 does not reproduce latest 1500 edge, 4 is one of the few with reliable top-end class/stable support.
7 has clearer 1200-specific current form than several rivals; alternative winner path exists if distance specificity dominates.

third_dispositions.reason: Most evidence-balanced top-three structure: winner 6, place reliability 4, 1200-specific top-3 horse 7.
1 has open-company form and can hold third if transfer adapts better than local lower-grade horses.
If 1200 tempo/position shape suits 7 better, 4 still retains durable third path.
Blends strongest winner with 1200 local place horse and class-tested transfer candidate.
Alternative structure if 4 improves enough to win while 6 remains safely in frame.

reasons: Full inherited v2.0 venue canon text not supplied; only v2.1 addendum available, so coverage is partial.
Numerical authority is NOT_READY; no bound production component score rules, forcing evidence-only qualitative ordering.
First-day/early-meeting style bias is not strongly established; same-day races provide limited support and cannot be over-generalized.
Several runners are lightly raced 2yo fillies, increasing progression and volatility uncertainty.
No official universal training comment/paddock data beyond stated missingness.

unresolved: Exact separation between 4 and 7 for P2 is close: 4 stronger stable/overall solidity, 7 stronger recent 1200 local line.
Exact third ordering among 1 and 3 remains partially unresolved; 1 has tougher outside-company evidence, 3 has stronger trainer/jockey upside.
Back-end ordering among 8,12,10,11 is low-confidence because evidence mostly negative rather than positively discriminative.
Independent P3 path for 7 is strong enough that a different role serialization could also be defended.
prediction.evidence_conflict: Official market favors 6 clearly and then 4, with 7/1/3 in the next cluster; qualitative reading mostly aligns, but 1 is elevated over 3 on class-exposure/third-path grounds despite 3's stronger connections.
prediction.market_conflict: LOW: market and evidence both center 6/4/7 as principal contenders, though exact placement of 1 and 3 differs slightly from odds ordering.

venue_prediction_context.interpretation: FNB v2.1 context read qualitatively only: current track state is only lightly informed by same-day races, so no hard bias declared. Preference is given to runners with lower stage-cost routes into the first flight at Funabashi, proven local 1200/1500 handling, and credible top-3 maintenance rather than late unsupported rescue. 6 owns the cleanest winner path, 4/7 are strongest local reachability rivals, and 1 is the main transfer horse with open-company evidence.
